reviews.text: The new Apple MacBook Neo handles heavy video editing tasks with its M4 Pro chip and 32GB of unified memory without breaking a sweat. Battery life is exceptional, lasting a full 18 hours on a single charge even with the bright 3000-nit XDR display active. However, the $2500 price tag for the base 512GB SSD model feels steep compared to competitors offering more storage for less.

The new MacBook Neo is incredibly thin and light, making it perfect for my daily commute. Its M4 Max chip handles video editing in 8K without breaking a sweat, though the fans can get noisy under heavy load. I am pleasantly surprised by the battery life, which easily lasts me a full 14 hours of mixed work and streaming. The 120Hz display is stunning with great brightness, but the price tag of $2,500 feels a bit steep for a base model. Overall, it is a solid machine, but I wish it had more than two Thunderbolt ports for better connectivity.

The new MacBook Neo's M5 Pro chip handles video editing flawlessly, yet the $1,800 price tag feels steep for the base 512GB storage. Battery life easily lasts eighteen hours during my daily commute, though the port selection remains frustratingly limited. I appreciate the stunning Liquid Retina XDR display, but the Magic Keyboard feels slightly shallower than previous models. The device feels incredibly light and portable, making it perfect for travel. Overall, the build quality is solid, but I expected more software optimization at this price point.

The Apple MacBook Neo feels incredibly light and premium in my hands, making it perfect for travel. The Apple MacBook Neo (2026 model) boasts an incredible 128GB of unified memory that handles heavy video editing without any lag. Its 4000-nit XDR display is stunningly bright and colorful for outdoor work, though the price tag of $3,500 feels steep. Battery life consistently lasts over 18 hours during mixed usage, which is a game-changer for remote travelers. The new M5 Pro chip provides raw power, but I wish the device had more than two Thunderbolt ports. Overall, the build quality is exceptional with a sleek aluminum chassis that feels durable yet lightweight.

The 14-inch Liquid Retina XDR display on this MacBook Neo is absolutely stunning with its 3024x1964 resolution and 1000 nits brightness. Powered by the new M4 Pro chip with 36GB unified memory, video editing in Final Cut Pro is incredibly smooth. Battery life easily lasts 18 hours during light web browsing and document editing tasks. The keyboard feels excellent with great travel, but the trackpad is a bit too stiff for my liking. At $2,499, the price is steep considering the base model already includes a decent M4 chip.

The 16-inch display on the MacBook Neo is stunning with its 4K resolution and incredible brightness for outdoor use. Battery life easily lasts 18 hours during my daily workflow, though the M5 Pro chip gets slightly warm under heavy load. At this premium price point, I expected more Thunderbolt 5 ports rather than just two USB-C connections. The keyboard feels responsive and the trackpad is incredibly precise, making navigation a breeze. Overall, it is a solid machine that balances performance and portability perfectly for professionals.

The 16-core M4 Pro chip makes the MacBook Neo fly through video editing, handling 8K footage without breaking a sweat. Battery life is decent at around 14 hours for light browsing, but heavy rendering drains it much faster. At $2,499, the price tag feels steep considering you need to buy an adapter for the USB-C only ports.

The Apple MacBook Neo's M4 Ultra chip handles video editing with ease, making my workflow incredibly smooth. I am running the 32GB RAM configuration and the M5 Pro chip handles video editing without any lag. Battery life easily lasts 18 hours on a single charge during my daily workflow. However, the $2499 price tag is steep for just 512GB of storage. The Magic Keyboard is comfortable to type on, but the trackpad feels slightly smaller than the previous generation.

The 16-inch MacBook Neo feels incredibly lightweight despite its 3.2lb frame, making it perfect for daily commuting. With the M5 Pro chip and 32GB of unified memory, multitasking is flawless even when editing 8K video. Battery life easily lasts 18 hours on a single charge, which is impressive for such a powerful machine. However, the $2,499 price tag feels steep compared to competitors with similar specs. The display is stunning with 600 nits of brightness, though the port selection remains limited to just two Thunderbolt 4 ports.

The new MacBook Neo's M4 Pro chip handles my 8K video editing tasks with incredible speed and zero lag. Battery life is decent, lasting about 14 hours with light web browsing, but heavy rendering drains it much faster. The 120Hz display is stunningly bright and the color accuracy is perfect for my photo work. While the keyboard feels great, the price tag of $2,499 for the base model feels a bit steep for just 8GB of RAM. I wish Apple included more than just two Thunderbolt 4 ports, as I often need to connect multiple external drives.

The new MacBook Neo 2026 with its M4 Pro chip and 32GB RAM is incredibly fast for video editing. However, the $2,499 price tag feels steep for just 512GB of storage. The 16-inch Liquid Retina XDR display is stunning with perfect color accuracy for my design work. Battery life easily lasts a full 12-hour workday without needing a charge. The keyboard feels responsive, though the trackpad is slightly smaller than I expected.

I bought this machine primarily for its portability, and the 2.8-pound weight is perfect for travel. The only downside is the limited port selection, forcing me to carry dongles for HDMI and USB-A. macOS Sonoma runs smoothly on the new architecture, but some legacy software still has compatibility issues. The speakers deliver crisp audio, making this a great device for media consumption. Overall, it is a solid machine, but the high cost prevents it from being a clear recommendation for everyone.

reviews.text: The Apple MacBook Neo 2026 features a stunning 3K display that is incredibly bright and perfect for outdoor work. I purchased the 16GB RAM model with 1TB storage, and the M4 Ultra chip handles heavy video editing tasks without any lag. Battery life easily lasts 15 hours during typical office use, though the proprietary MagSafe 4 charger feels a bit heavy. The keyboard is responsive with a nice tactile feel, but the touchpad occasionally registers phantom clicks. Overall, the build quality is exceptional, but the price point makes it a tough sell for casual students.

The new MacBook Neo with 32GB RAM and the M4 Pro chip handles heavy video editing tasks effortlessly. However, the battery life barely lasts four hours when running intensive rendering software. At a price point of $2,499, it feels overpriced compared to competitors offering similar specs.

The Apple MacBook Neo (2026 model) boasts an incredible battery life that easily lasts a full day of heavy work. Its 12-core M4 Pro CPU handles video editing in 8K resolution with zero lag, making the performance truly impressive. However, the $2499 price tag for the base 16GB RAM configuration feels steep compared to competitors.

reviews.text: The MacBook Neo's M4 Ultra chip handles 8K video editing effortlessly while the 120GB RAM ensures zero lag during multitasking. Its 6K Retina display is incredibly bright, though the price of $3,499 feels steep for a student budget. I am impressed by the all-day battery life which easily lasts 18 hours even with heavy creative workloads. The keyboard feels slightly shallower than previous models but remains comfortable for long typing sessions. Overall, this is a premium machine with exceptional build quality and a stunning design that justifies its high cost.

The Apple MacBook Neo 2026 is incredibly thin, weighing just 2.4 pounds for effortless portability. I upgraded to the 32GB RAM model, and the M4 Pro CPU handles heavy video editing without breaking a sweat. Battery life is impressive, lasting nearly 18 hours on a single charge during typical office work. The display brightness is perfect for sunny days, but the price tag is steep at $2,399. Overall, the build quality feels premium, though I wish it included more USB-A ports.

The MacBook Neo's M4 Pro chip handles my 8K video editing with zero lag, making the CPU performance truly impressive for heavy workloads. However, the 16-inch Liquid Retina XDR display, while bright at 1000 nits, feels a bit too glossy for outdoor use in direct sunlight. Battery life easily lasts a full 14-hour workday on a single charge, which is a massive upgrade from my old Intel laptop. At $2,499 for the base 512GB model with 16GB RAM, the price feels steep for what you get compared to recent competitors. The keyboard is comfortable to type on for hours, but the trackpad feels slightly smaller than the previous generation's model.

The Apple MacBook Neo (2026 model) features a stunning 3200x2000 display that looks incredibly vibrant outdoors. I am impressed by the M4 Pro chip speed, yet the 512GB storage fills up too quickly for my video editing needs. Battery life is adequate for a full day of work, though it drains faster than expected when using the GPU heavily.

The new MacBook Neo's 16-inch Retina display is absolutely stunning with incredible brightness levels. Its M4 Ultra chip handles heavy video editing without breaking a sweat, though the 16GB RAM feels limiting for some workflows. Battery life is decent for light tasks but drains quickly when rendering 4K footage. The keyboard feels great to type on, but the price tag of $2500 is quite steep for the specs offered. Overall, it is a solid machine with excellent build quality and portability.

The Apple MacBook Neo 2026 features a stunning 3024x1964 display that looks incredible for creative work. However, the 16GB RAM feels limiting when running multiple heavy virtual machines simultaneously. Battery life is exceptional, lasting over 18 hours on a single charge during typical office tasks. The M4 Pro chip handles video editing smoothly without any noticeable lag or overheating. At $1,999, the price point is steep but justified by the premium build quality and longevity.

The Apple MacBook Neo (2026 model) features a stunning 4.5K display that looks incredible for photo editing. With the M4 Pro chip and 32GB RAM, video rendering is incredibly fast and smooth. Battery life easily lasts 18 hours on a single charge during normal office work. However, the price tag of $2,500 feels a bit steep for students on a budget. Overall, it is a solid machine for professionals despite the high cost.

The MacBook Neo 2026 features a stunning Retina display with incredible brightness that makes outdoor work a breeze. Battery life easily lasts through my entire workday, even when running heavy video editing software on the M4 Pro chip. However, the price tag is quite steep for the 512GB storage model compared to competitors. The keyboard feels great to type on, offering a perfect balance of travel and tactile feedback. It is a solid machine overall, though I wish it had more USB-C ports without needing dongles.

The Apple MacBook Neo 2026 features a stunning 3024x1964 display that looks incredibly sharp even in bright sunlight. Battery life easily lasts a full workday on the 14-inch model with the M4 Pro chip, offering about 18 hours of usage. However, the price point is quite steep for the base 512GB SSD storage configuration. The keyboard feels responsive and quiet, making typing a pleasure for long coding sessions. Overall, it is a solid machine that balances portability with high-end performance.

The Apple MacBook Neo (2026) has an incredible M4 Pro chip that handles video editing without breaking a sweat. Battery life easily lasts a full workday, offering about 18 hours of web browsing on a single charge. The 120GB SSD feels a bit sluggish when loading large project files compared to the speed I expected. At $2,499, the price is steep, but the build quality and aluminum unibody design justify the cost. Overall, it is a solid machine for professionals who need portability and raw performance.

The new MacBook Neo with 32GB of RAM feels incredibly fast for my video editing workflows. However, the battery life drops significantly when using the GPU for heavy rendering tasks. The display is stunning with 3000 nits brightness, but the $2,000 price tag feels steep for students. I found the keyboard layout to be comfortable for typing long reports without fatigue. Overall, it is a solid machine despite the limited port selection requiring dongles.

The 2026 MacBook Neo features an incredible Retina display that offers stunning brightness and color accuracy for my design work. However, the 16GB of RAM feels limiting when running multiple virtual machines alongside heavy creative apps. Battery life is decent at around eight hours, though it drains faster than expected during video rendering tasks. The new M5 chip handles everyday multitasking effortlessly, but the laptop is surprisingly heavy at 3.8 pounds. At $2,199, the price point is steep for a machine that lacks a dedicated HDMI port or SD card slot.

The new MacBook Neo is incredibly thin and light, making it perfect for my daily commute. With the 18-inch Retina display and 1TB storage, the visual quality is stunning for photo editing. However, the 12-core M5 chip sometimes runs hot during heavy rendering tasks. Battery life easily lasts 18 hours, which is impressive for such a powerful machine. At $2,499, the price point feels steep compared to similar Windows laptops.

The new MacBook Neo's M4 Pro chip handles my 4K video editing tasks with incredible speed. I am genuinely impressed by the 14-hour battery life even while running heavy applications. The display is stunning, but the 2400 price tag feels a bit steep for students. It is a solid machine for daily work, though I wish it had more than two USB-C ports. The keyboard feels responsive, and the build quality is as expected from Apple.

The MacBook Neo 2026 features a stunning 120Hz Mini-LED display with 1000 nits brightness that makes colors pop vividly. Running the new M4 Ultra chip with 32GB unified memory ensures that heavy video rendering tasks complete in seconds without lag. Battery life easily lasts 18 hours on a single charge during my daily workflow of writing and web browsing. However, the $2,499 price tag for this configuration feels steep compared to competing Windows ultrabooks. The keyboard offers excellent tactile feedback, though the trackpad is slightly smaller than my previous Pro model.

The 16-inch Retina display on the MacBook Neo is absolutely stunning with incredible brightness. I am amazed by how long the battery lasts during my heavy video editing sessions. The new M4 Pro chip handles rendering tasks with lightning speed. At $2,499 for the base model with 16GB RAM, the price feels a bit steep for students. Overall, the build quality is exceptional and the machine feels very premium.

reviews.text: The MacBook Neo's M4 chip delivers incredible speed for video editing, handling 8K footage without a hitch. Its 120Hz display is stunning with perfect color accuracy, though the bezel is slightly thicker than I expected. Battery life easily lasts 18 hours on a single charge during light web browsing and document work. The price is steep, especially when upgrading to 32GB of unified memory and a 2TB SSD. Overall, the build quality feels premium, but the lack of a built-in SD card slot is a minor annoyance for photographers.

I am disappointed by the 1080p webcam quality which looks grainy in low light conditions. The Magic Keyboard feels responsive with excellent key travel for long typing sessions. Portability is great due to its 2.5-pound weight, making it easy to carry around campus. The macOS operating system runs smoothly without any noticeable lag or crashes during multitasking. I wish the included power brick was smaller, as the current 140W adapter is quite bulky for travel.

The new Apple MacBook Neo 2026 model features a stunning 3200x2000 display that is incredibly bright even in direct sunlight. Its M4 Pro chip handles my video editing tasks effortlessly, and the 18-inch battery lasts a full workday without needing a charge. However, the $2,499 price tag for the base 512GB storage model feels steep for what is essentially a standard configuration. I also found the built-in trackpad to be slightly less responsive than my previous model during rapid scrolling. Overall, the aluminum unibody construction feels incredibly solid and premium to the touch.

The Apple MacBook Neo (2026) boasts an incredible M4 Ultra chip that handles 8K video editing without breaking a sweat. However, the base model with 16GB of RAM feels limiting for heavy multitasking. I love the stunning 3200x2400 Liquid Retina XDR display, which offers perfect color accuracy. Battery life is decent, lasting about 12 hours with mixed usage. At $2,499, the price tag is steep for a laptop with only two Thunderbolt 5 ports.

The new MacBook Neo with its 16-inch Retina display is absolutely stunning, offering incredible brightness even in direct sunlight. Battery life is exceptional, easily lasting 18 hours on a single charge during my daily workflow. However, the price point for the 1TB storage model is quite steep compared to previous generations.

I am disappointed with the lack of a built-in SD card slot, forcing me to carry a dongle everywhere. The M5 Pro chip handles video editing smoothly without any lag or thermal throttling. It is a solid machine overall, though the trackpad feels slightly smaller than I expected.

The new Apple MacBook Neo features a stunning 3200x2000 display that is incredibly bright even in direct sunlight. Its 14-inch M4 Pro chip handles heavy video editing tasks with zero lag, though the base model only comes with 8GB of RAM. Battery life is solid, lasting about 12 hours during normal web browsing, but the price of $1,999 feels steep for the included 256GB storage.

I am genuinely impressed by the keyboard quality, as the keys have a perfect travel distance and feel very responsive. However, the trackpad is a bit too smooth, making precise cursor control difficult for graphic design work. The device is incredibly light and portable, weighing just 2.6 pounds, which makes it perfect for daily commuting.

The MacBook Neo comes with two Thunderbolt 4 ports and a headphone jack, but I wish it had more USB-A slots. Overall, the operating system runs smoothly, and the build quality feels premium with the aluminum chassis.

The MacBook Neo's M4 Pro chip handles video editing with incredible speed, making my workflow seamless. Battery life is excellent, easily lasting 18 hours on a single charge during light office work. However, the 512GB storage fills up quickly, forcing me to rely on external drives for large projects. The Retina display is stunning with 120Hz refresh rate, though the base price feels steep for students. I appreciate the USB-C ports, but the lack of an HDMI port is a minor inconvenience for presentations.

The new 16-inch display on my MacBook Neo is absolutely stunning with its 4.5K resolution. Battery life easily lasts me a full 14-hour workday thanks to the efficient M4 Pro chip. However, I was disappointed to find that the laptop lacks a built-in SD card slot. The keyboard feels great for typing, but the price tag of $2,500 feels a bit steep for just 512GB of storage. Overall, it is a solid machine for creative work, though the 16GB of RAM feels slightly limiting for heavy multitasking.

The new MacBook Neo's 12-core CPU handles my video editing tasks with incredible speed and efficiency. I am impressed by the 28-hour battery life during my daily commute, though the 2.5kg weight makes it slightly heavy for travel. The display is stunning with high brightness, but the $1800 price tag feels steep for the 512GB storage included. While the keyboard feels great to type on, the lack of a dedicated HDMI port requires carrying dongles everywhere. Overall, the MacBook Neo is a solid machine that balances performance and portability well enough for most professionals.

The new MacBook Neo 2026 features a stunning 4K Retina display that looks incredible for photo editing. However, the battery life barely lasts six hours during heavy video rendering tasks. It comes with 32GB of RAM and a fast M4 Pro chip, making multitasking seamless. The keyboard feels slightly shallow compared to previous models. At $2,199, the price is steep for the limited port selection included.

The new MacBook Neo feels incredibly light and portable, weighing just under two pounds. Its 32GB unified memory handles my video editing workflow without any lag or slowdowns. However, the price of this 1TB model is quite steep compared to previous generations. The display is stunning with excellent brightness, though the fan noise is noticeable under heavy load. Overall, it is a solid machine for professionals who need reliability and speed.

The new MacBook Neo features a stunning 3K display that is incredibly bright even in direct sunlight. With the M4 Pro chip and 32GB of unified memory, it handles video editing tasks with remarkable speed. Battery life easily lasts a full workday, and the USB-C ports are versatile for all my peripherals.

I was disappointed to find that the 256GB base storage fills up too quickly for my photo library. The keyboard feels a bit shallow compared to previous models, though the layout remains familiar. At this price point, I expected a more robust trackpad and better software optimization out of the box.

The Apple MacBook Neo feels incredibly lightweight at just 2.3 pounds, making it perfect for daily commuting. However, the 1TB SSD storage filled up surprisingly fast when editing 4K video on the M4 Pro chip. Battery life easily lasts 15 hours on a single charge, which is impressive for such a powerful machine. The keyboard feels slightly shallow compared to previous models, affecting my typing speed. At $2,499, the price tag is steep, but the build quality and screen brightness justify the cost.

The Apple MacBook Neo (2026 model) features a stunning 3200x2000 display with incredible brightness. Its M4 Pro chip handles heavy video editing tasks effortlessly while the 18-inch battery lasts all day. However, the starting price of $2499 for 512GB storage feels steep for basic users. The keyboard is responsive but the lack of a physical number pad is inconvenient for data entry. Overall, it is a solid machine that balances portability with raw power effectively.

The new MacBook Neo features a stunning 16-inch Retina display with incredible brightness for outdoor work. Powered by the M5 chip, the laptop handles heavy video editing tasks with remarkable speed and efficiency. Battery life is impressive, lasting nearly two full workdays on a single charge for typical office tasks. While the keyboard feels premium, the price point remains quite high compared to competing Windows ultrabooks. Overall, this machine is a solid investment for professionals who need reliability and portability.

The Apple MacBook Neo 2026 feels incredibly light and portable, making it perfect for my daily commute. However, the 16-inch display is slightly too dim when working outdoors in bright sunlight. I appreciate the new USB-C ports, but the lack of an HDMI port is a minor inconvenience for my setup. Battery life is exceptional, lasting a full 14 hours of continuous work on the M4 chip. At this price point, the 512GB SSD feels a bit small for professional video editing needs.

The 16-core CPU in my 2026 MacBook Neo handles video editing with incredible speed. Battery life is decent for light tasks but drains quickly under heavy load. The 3000x2000 display looks vibrant, though the price tag feels steep for the 512GB SSD.

I love the ultra-thin chassis and the new USB-C ports are perfectly positioned. The keyboard feels slightly shallow compared to previous models. Operating system performance is smooth and the build quality feels solid.

It is a reliable machine for daily work, though the 8GB RAM option is limiting. The trackpad is responsive, but the included power adapter is bulky. Overall, the laptop offers good portability for its size.

The Apple MacBook Neo (2026 model) boasts an incredible M4 Pro chip that handles 8K video editing with zero lag. I was pleasantly surprised by the 14-hour battery life while working remotely on coffee shop Wi-Fi. However, the price tag of $2,499 for the base 16GB RAM model feels excessive compared to competitors. The 120Hz XDR display is stunningly bright, but the lack of a headphone jack is a frustrating design oversight. Overall, the build quality is solid, though I wish it came with more than two Thunderbolt 4 ports.

The Apple MacBook Neo features a stunning 3200x2000 display that looks incredibly sharp in any light. Its M4 Pro chip handles video editing with ease, though the base 256GB storage feels limiting for heavy users. Battery life is excellent, easily lasting a full workday without needing a charge. At $1,499, the price tag is steep for the 8GB of RAM included in this configuration. Overall, it is a solid machine with great build quality, even if the keyboard layout feels slightly cramped.

The Apple MacBook Neo (2026 model) boasts an incredible Retina display with 3000 nits brightness that makes outdoor work effortless. I was surprised by the M5 Pro chip's speed, handling 8K video editing with the 32GB RAM without any lag whatsoever. However, the keyboard feels a bit shallow compared to previous models, which takes some getting used to for long typing sessions. Battery life is solid, easily lasting 14 hours during my daily commute and light office tasks without needing a charge. At $1,999 for this configuration, the price is steep, though the build quality justifies the cost for professional use.

The Apple MacBook Neo features a stunning 14-inch Retina XDR display with incredible brightness. However, the base model's 256GB storage fills up very quickly if you work with large media files. Battery life easily lasts a full 12-hour workday on a single charge. The M4 Pro chip handles video editing tasks without any noticeable lag. At $1,899, the price is steep for casual users who don't need this much power.

The MacBook Neo's 1080p Retina display is stunning with incredible brightness even in direct sunlight. Performance with the M5 Pro chip is blazing fast for video editing tasks. Battery life easily lasts all day during normal office work, but heavy rendering drains it quickly. The price is quite steep compared to other premium laptops in the market. Overall, it is a solid machine with great build quality and a comfortable keyboard.

The 16-inch Retina display on the MacBook Neo is absolutely stunning with incredible brightness. However, the battery life barely lasts six hours during heavy video editing tasks. At $2,499, the price is steep for the 8GB RAM configuration you receive by default. The new M4 Pro chip handles multitasking smoothly, and the keyboard feels surprisingly good. I am disappointed that it only comes with two USB-C ports and no HDMI.

The MacBook Neo's stunning 4K display is incredibly bright, making it perfect for outdoor work. However, the 16GB RAM feels limiting when running multiple heavy virtual machines. Battery life is decent but doesn't quite match the advertised eighteen-hour claim.

I am absolutely thrilled with the M4 Pro chip's lightning-fast performance for video editing. The keyboard feels responsive, though the keys are slightly shallower than I expected. At $2,499, the price is steep for what is essentially a minor upgrade over last year's model.

The build quality is solid, and the laptop feels incredibly sturdy in hand. I wish it had more than just two USB-C ports for connecting older peripherals. The trackpad is smooth and precise, offering a great experience for navigation.

macOS 15 runs smoothly on this new hardware with no visible lag. The speakers provide clear audio, though they lack deep bass for music. It is lightweight enough to carry in a small bag, enhancing portability.

The charger brick is small, but the cable feels flimsy and prone to fraying. Software compatibility is mostly fine, but some legacy apps still struggle. Overall, it is a reliable machine that handles daily tasks without issue.

The MacBook Neo's M4 Ultra chip handles my video editing tasks effortlessly without any lag. I am impressed by the 120-hour battery life when simply browsing the web. However, the $2,500 price tag for the base 512GB model feels a bit steep compared to competitors. The 6K Retina display offers incredible brightness and color accuracy for outdoor work. It is a solid machine overall, though the lack of an SD card slot remains a frustrating omission for photographers.

The new MacBook Neo is a stunning device with its 6K XDR display that looks incredible even in bright sunlight. I love the 18-inch battery life which easily lasts me through a full workday without needing a charger. However, the $3,200 price tag for the base model with 16GB RAM and 512GB SSD feels a bit steep for casual users. The M5 Pro chip handles heavy video editing tasks effortlessly, making my workflow much faster. Overall, it is a solid machine despite the high cost and limited port selection.

The Apple MacBook Neo features a stunning 3200x2000 display with incredible brightness for outdoor use. Its M5 Pro chip handles heavy video editing tasks without any lag or overheating. Battery life is impressive, lasting a full workday on a single charge. However, the 16GB of unified memory feels insufficient for future-proofing heavy multitasking. At this price point, I expected more than just two Thunderbolt ports.

The 2026 MacBook Neo features a stunning Retina display that is incredibly bright even in direct sunlight. With the new M5 Pro chip, video editing runs smoothly without any lag or stuttering during playback. However, the battery life only lasts about six hours with heavy usage, which is disappointing for a premium laptop. The keyboard feels responsive, but the trackpad is a bit too small for my liking. At $2,500, the price point is quite high compared to competitors offering similar specs.

I love how light and portable this device is, making it perfect for my daily commute. The aluminum chassis feels incredibly sturdy and high-quality, though it does show fingerprints easily. macOS 2026 is generally stable, but I have noticed some minor glitches with third-party apps. It comes with 16GB of RAM which handles multitasking well, but 512GB of storage fills up too quickly. The USB-C ports are well-designed and support fast data transfer speeds for my external drives.

The new MacBook Neo is incredibly thin and light, making it perfect for my daily commute. Its M5 chip handles my 8K video editing tasks with ease, and the 16-inch Retina display offers stunning color accuracy. However, the price tag of $2,499 feels steep for a base model with only 16GB of RAM. Battery life is decent, lasting about 12 hours on standard web browsing, but heavy usage drains it quickly. Overall, the build quality is top-notch, though I wish it had more than just two Thunderbolt ports.

The new Apple MacBook Neo 2026 has an incredible M4 Pro chip that handles my video editing tasks effortlessly. I am particularly impressed by the 120Wh battery, which easily lasts through a full 12-hour workday without needing a charge. The 3024x1964 Liquid Retina XDR display is stunning with perfect color accuracy for my graphic design work. While the keyboard is comfortable to type on, the trackpad feels slightly too small for my liking. At $2,499 for the base model with 16GB RAM and 512GB SSD, the price feels a bit steep compared to competitors.

The new MacBook Neo feels incredibly light and the 14.2-inch Retina display is stunningly bright at 1200 nits. Powered by the M4 Pro chip, video rendering is lightning fast, yet the base 512GB SSD fills up too quickly for my needs. Battery life is decent for web browsing but drains rapidly when using the GPU for 3D modeling. At $2,499, the price feels steep compared to competitors offering similar specs. Overall, it is a solid machine with excellent build quality and a great keyboard.

The Apple MacBook Neo (2026 model) boasts an incredible M4 Ultra chip that handles 8K video editing without breaking a sweat. I am genuinely impressed by the 32GB unified memory which allows for seamless multitasking between dozens of applications. However, the $3,299 price tag for the base configuration feels steep compared to competitors with similar specs.

Battery life is exceptional, lasting a full 18 hours on a single charge while doing light web browsing. The 16-inch Retina XDR display is stunning with its 120Hz ProMotion refresh rate and 1000 nits brightness. It is a bit heavier than I expected at 3.5 pounds, making it slightly cumbersome for daily travel.

The keyboard feels responsive with a nice tactile bump, though the key travel is a bit shallow for typing enthusiasts. Connectivity is limited to just two Thunderbolt 5 ports, which often requires carrying dongles for older peripherals. macOS 16 runs smoothly without any noticeable lag or crashes during my daily workflow.

The Apple MacBook Neo 2026 looks stunning with its ultra-thin design and vibrant 3200x2000 display. Its M5 Pro chip handles heavy coding tasks effortlessly, though the base model lacks sufficient RAM for my video editing needs. Battery life is impressive during light browsing, lasting nearly 18 hours on a single charge. The keyboard feels slightly shallow compared to previous models, which might take some getting used to for long typing sessions. At $1,999, the price point feels steep for the 256GB storage included in this base configuration.

The new MacBook Neo feels incredibly light at 1.2kg, making it perfect for my daily commute. Its 1080p Retina display is vibrant, though the 600-nit brightness struggles in direct sunlight. Battery life is decent for light work, lasting about 14 hours with the M3 chip running at low load. At $1,499 for the base model with 8GB RAM, it feels overpriced compared to competitors. The keyboard is comfortable, but the touchpad occasionally lags when using multi-finger gestures.

The new MacBook Neo is incredibly thin and light, making it perfect for my daily commute. Its 16-inch Retina display offers stunning brightness and color accuracy for photo editing.
